title: Saw-leaf Zelkova: Ancient Keyaki You Can Visit
meta_description: A queen rested under Seoul's 700-year zelkova while fleeing a mutiny in 1882. Three keyaki mapped, in Seoul, Kyoto and Florence.
intro: A Korean queen is recorded resting under one of these in 1882, in disguise, on her way out of a capital where soldiers had just stormed the palace over unpaid wages. The zelkova at Hwayang-dong is about 700 years old and has not moved since, twenty eight metres tall with a trunk seven and a half metres round. In Japan the species is keyaki, the timber temple carpenters and taiko drum makers reach for first, which is a decent explanation for why very large ones are uncommon. Kyoto's grows just inside one of the gates of the old palace enclosure and its age is a straight blank. Florence's has been measured three times in forty years, 3.30 metres round in 1980 and 4.40 in 2021, so you can watch it grow without waiting around.
